chunks: He is the First, for whom there was no 'before', so that there could be anything before Him,
and the Last, for whom there is no 'after', so that there could be anything after Him.
and the One who prevents the forgetfulness of the eyes from perceiving Him or comprehending Him,
Time does not change over Him, so as to admit of any change of condition about Him.
He is not in any place so as to allow Him movement (from one place to another).
If He gives away all that the mines of the mountains emit out or the shells of the ocean vomit out,
from the metal of gold and silver, and the scattering of pearls and the harvest of coral,
it would not affect his munificence, nor diminish the extent of what He has.
(In fact) He would still have such treasures of bounty as would not decrease by the demands of the creatures,
because He is that generous Being Whom the begging of beggars cannot make poor nor the pertinacity of beseechers make miser.
ai.seo_question: What are the divine attributes of God regarding time, space, and generosity according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: This passage from the 'Al-Ashbaah' chapter of Nahj al-Balagha employs rich metaphysical imagery to articulate the concept of *Tawhid* (Divine Oneness), specifically highlighting God's absolute transcendence (*Tanzih*) beyond temporal succession and spatial location. It further emphasizes His attribute of *Jawd* (generosity) by contrasting the finite nature of earthly treasures—such as the metals of mountains and pearls of seas—with the inexhaustible divine bounty that never diminishes despite the demands of creation.
